review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves a substantive sound-and-complete coupled law-set criterion through exact mixing realization, finite source partitions, simultaneous response matrices, and real-algebraic elimination, but it does not solve the advertised structural question of when separate regime equivalence implies joint equivalence: prop:marginal-joint-gluing-criterion reduces this to existence of one common observational root, while oeq:separate-versus-joint leaves realizability and a separating graph pair open. The delivered population class also drops the brief's centering and finite-second-moment restrictions; equivalence for this larger moment-free class does not logically imply equivalence for the requested restricted law sets, although the diagnostic argument appears adaptable by centering its Bernoulli sources. The explicit bit-operation bounds are not established by the cited quantifier-elimination theorem as written: the citation supplies asymptotic arithmetic complexity and intermediate bit-size bounds, whereas the manuscript asserts a particular closed-form bit bound and certificate output without deriving the conversion. These scope and complexity gaps, together with the absence of a worked compiler or substantive perturbational application, constrain the paper below a flagship contribution despite the field-level core theorem. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned `revise` and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound — do not bank it as downgraded on this verdict alone. Open findings: redundant_assumption@ass:source-centering, positioning_missing@thm:effective-population-compiler, related_work_incomplete@thm:graph-confidence-superset
